effect_mechanism: Mangrove planting reaches people mainly through aquatic products, and the returns on the planting itself are reported as benefit-cost appraisals. In northern Viet Nam mangroves had a positive impact on additional income for coastal communities through an increase in per hectare yield of aquaculture products such as shells and oyster by 209-789 per cent [ev_household_income_ifrc11_1] - value that accrues to the households harvesting them - and the project's cost-benefit analysis gives commune benefit-cost ratios of 3.06 to 68.92 excluding ecological benefits and 28.86 to 104.96 including them [ev_economic_return_ifrc11_1, ev_economic_return_ifrc11_2]. A global meta-analysis of mangrove restoration reports benefit-cost ratios of 10.50 to 6.83 across discount rates when summing benefits by ecosystem service, and 3.36 to 2.19 using the mean total economic benefit [ev_economic_return_su21_1]; a cited study concludes that the benefits of mangrove reforestation projects outweigh their costs [ev_economic_return_hernmel17_1]. WOCAT compilers rate food security and self-sufficiency in Senegal and the risk of production failure in Bangladesh as improved, and rate the long-term cost-benefit of both establishment and maintenance in Bangladesh as positive [ev_food_security_wocat_1442_2011_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_food_security_wocat_4300_2019_risk_of_production_failure, ev_economic_return_wocat_4300_2019_costbenefit_establishment_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_4300_2019_costbenefit_maintenance_long]. A World Bank study for coastal Bangladesh models livelihood benefits of mangrove restoration at 3,700 to 86,000 USD per hectare, with regional means of 22,039 to 30,330 USD per hectare [ev_economic_return_wbmang25_1]. A second-hand reading of an economic model for three coastal districts of northern Vietnam finds mangrove restoration desirable from an economic perspective based solely on the direct benefits of use by local communities [ev_frmg_erw09_1], and on Mexico's Gulf coast the mangrove reforestation investments at both pilot sites had positive net present values at all three discount rates considered [ev_frmg_mxicr_1].
conditionality: Nothing here observes household income or poverty against a counterfactual: the outcome is reached through proxies - economic return, food security and reported income gains - and the strongest numbers are project appraisals rather than measured welfare. The 209-789 per cent is a yield increase of aquaculture products, not an income change [ev_household_income_ifrc11_1]. The Viet Nam ratios come from an evaluation commissioned by the implementer, model costs and benefits forward, and the higher ratios include ecological benefits the source says had yet to materialise [ev_economic_return_ifrc11_1, ev_economic_return_ifrc11_2]; the meta-analysis pools unpaired benefit and cost samples, mostly from East and Southeast Asian planting projects [ev_economic_return_su21_1]; the Bangladesh livelihood values are modelled present values transferred from a global valuation meta-regression, not observed income, and come from grey literature [ev_economic_return_wbmang25_1]. The Vietnam model is cited second-hand and described by the citing author as preliminary [ev_frmg_erw09_1]. The Mexico result is the project's own completion report, its benefits projected forward from planting on former cattle pasture rather than observed, with coastal protection and carbon not valued [ev_frmg_mxicr_1]. The WOCAT units are compiler ratings, and the review finding is a conclusion cited from another study [ev_economic_return_hernmel17_1]. Two cost findings are kept out of the direction because the saving goes to society, not to households: mangrove restoration projects reported a median cost of US$0.1 per square metre (range 0.05–6.43) and an average replacement cost ratio of 5 (95% CI 3.1–6.9) against submerged breakwaters giving the same wave reduction, and depending on the water depth, mangrove projects in Vietnam can be three to five times cheaper than a breakwater [ev_frmg_nara16_3, ev_frmg_nara16_4]. That comparison assumed far lower breakwater construction costs in Vietnam than in Europe or the USA, applies only to small waves, and the authors note such defences are not always cost effective [ev_frmg_nara16_4]. A third Mexican figure is kept out of the direction because its value goes to society, not to households: the cost-benefit table for the two Gulf-coast pilot sites attributes $50,866 pesos/ha/year of improved water quantity and quality to each hectare of reforested mangrove [ev_mgM_mxicr_1]. It is a model input, not a measurement at the sites: the completion report says the per-hectare values come from an earlier Mexican valuation study, updated, and the report is the lender's own self-evaluation. The same table shows how little the stand itself pays its neighbours: forest products are valued at $98 pesos/ha/year, against $20,031 pesos/ha/year for improved fisheries habitat, so any income case rests on the water and fishery services rather than on anything harvested from the trees.
